notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/pcdshub__ophyd-ads --backend fake; the evidence is contract_checked and never an MHS-Device level. No PLC, ADS library, ophyd or pyads code was imported or run, no ADS connection was opened, and the hardware backend was never loaded. The clone at 2029e0bebee6148aba47e5947467574337fea61a was only read; its git status is clean. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes OphydDriver with ophyd_ads.devices:NcAxis, but every NcAxis field is Component(AdsSignal, ...) and AdsSignal is a custom Signal subclass (ophyd_ads/signal.py:32), not one of the classic EpicsSignal/EpicsSignalRO/Signal declarations the Ophyd source proof accepts. This package is therefore a direct Driver over the same card entry class NcAxis (ophyd_ads/devices.py:7) with a native.py factory; gate G7 proved the fake and the native surface against that class. Covered: the eleven telemetry channels the card names (act_acc, act_pos, act_pos_modulo, act_torque, act_velo, axis_state, cmd_no, control_d_word, couple_state, ctrl_output, drive_output), each as a read-only @read field and as a member of the cap.sensing.read.v1 action. Every read is a fresh AdsSignal.get (ophyd_ads/signal.py:72-78) and Symbol.read (ophyd_ads/ads.py:206-210), not a monitor cache; the optional fields input selects a subset. A name outside the eleven channels contributes no value, so the catalogue class example fields ["temperature"] completes with an empty values object rather than a fabricated reading. No write, setpoint, subscription or ADS notification is exposed. NOT COVERED: set_acc, set_pos, set_pos_modulo, set_torque and set_velo (Component(AdsSignal, ...) at ophyd_ads/devices.py:25-29), which would write a motion setpoint through AdsSignal.put (ophyd_ads/signal.py:80-83); the package has no native axis stop and no sourced position/velocity bound, so it does not expose that path. Also NOT COVERED: err_state, homing_state, override_v, pos_diff, pos_diff_couple and state_d_word (ophyd_ads/devices.py:19, 21-24, 30), the commented-out from_plc/to_plc declarations (ophyd_ads/devices.py:20, 31), the AdsSignal.subscribe subscription path (ophyd_ads/signal.py:91-100), and every hardware behaviour. Units: no line of the clone states an engineering unit, scale or axis meaning, so the fields carry no unit and the deployment's TwinCAT symbol configuration supplies the meaning. Safety: R0 read-only; no native stop is declared. Plc.stop only stops the Python client's queue thread and closes the ADS connection (ophyd_ads/ads.py:298-300, 324-333) and sends no stop command to the PLC; it is not claimed as an axis stop. An MHS e-stop engages the endpoint's software latch and stops nothing physical; reads remain available. The R2/R3 loader refusal of an unsigned model-written hardware backend is not claimed here because this package is R0, and no hardware run is claimed at any risk. Hardware backend: native.py builds NcAxis(prefix=<deployment ADS address>, name=<operator name>) and was never run; a deployment must supply the ADS address and symbol prefix and validate ophyd, pyads, the TwinCAT symbol types and the PLC network path. The package is model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, reviewed_by is null, and no human reviewed or tested it. Gate notes: G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is a warning because the driver declares no limits (CL2), which is correct for a read-only integration with no numeric input; no other gate warning was reported. The clone's upstream test directory (ophyd_ads/tests) contains only __init__.py and conftest.py, so G9 found no upstream test functions to run. Licence: BSD-3-Clause, matching the clone LICENSE and setup.py:48.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation against the readiness evidence (blocked for OphydDriver: the custom AdsSignal, ophyd_ads/signal.py:32): a read-only R0 profile of the card's own entry class NcAxis (devices.py:7) is the honest subset the addendum names. Every served channel is a direct Component (8-18) read with AdsSignal.get, a fresh Symbol.read over ADS (signal.py:72-78, ads.py:206-210); no set_* setpoint, put, subscription or Plc.stop (a client-thread shutdown, not an axis stop, ads.py:298-300, 324-333) is bound; native.py builds NcAxis(prefix, name) and writes nothing. Every fact was read against its lines; one said more than its range ('for TwinCAT NC axis values' on devices.py:7-18) and was narrowed, with the TwinCAT statement added as a README fact (README.rst:12). The reviewer changed driver.py and facts.md and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged (sha256:b6ad31fb5d7cf533ab56a052c1e1d92215fd11b1baab24b1a4c4c5a1028956f5). Override proposal: direct-driver python-object. For the human reviewer: Building NcAxis constructs all 22 AdsSignals, including the five set_* setpoints (never written), and opens the process-wide ADS connection with a daemon thread (ads.py:269-280, 340-348); the driver has no teardown, so the connection stays open until the process exits. Value types and meaning come from the deployment's TwinCAT symbols; a BOOL or array symbol would fail the number fields.
